title: Grants for Clark County
lead: Grant programs that match budget lines and records on this site. Matching is by County Commons; check eligibility with the agency.

fits.text: USDA Community Facilities lists prisons, community gardens, community kitchens and greenhouses as eligible; its loans run up to 40 years with a grant share. Opioid settlement money has no deadline.
The state’s County Courthouse Restoration Grant is open for letters of intent, with applications due January 27, 2027.
USDA’s rural water loans are limited to towns of 10,000 people or fewer. State revolving fund loans also carry federal lead-pipe and PFAS money. The city’s lead pipe inventory is Docket #15.
The Rural Services Block Grant (due October 16) pays up to $100,000 with a 10% match for towns under 3,000. FEMA’s firefighter grants go straight to departments about once a year.

src.label: Arkansas Economic Development — Rural Services Block Grant

fits.text: USDA’s self-help housing program pays a nonprofit to guide families who build each other’s homes. It needs a nonprofit sponsor.

not_available: Delta Regional Authority grants: Clark County is not in its region.
USDA rural water loans for Arkadelphia itself: the city is over the 10,000-person limit (other water systems in the county may qualify).

already.text: The county’s last audit (2023) shows about $3.44 million in state aid — mostly road money — and about $0.3 million in federal aid.
The 2026 budget still carries $471,142 of federal pandemic relief (ARPA) money. How much the county received in all, and how it was spent, isn’t documented on this site yet (Docket #19).
The economic development corporation (EDCCC) won state site-development grants of $1,013,710 (December 2024) and $3,792,543 (April 2026) for the industrial site near Gum Springs.

help.text: The West Central Arkansas Planning and Development District lists Clark County in its service area and guides cities and counties through grant applications.
